neighbours.label: word-final piece 'by' right after a short '-i-' stem piece (bil|by, tril|by, Bix|by, Bib|by, Dig|by); not 'by' in other names
fire: The greater bilby digs long burrows in the desert sand.
A colony of the rare bilby was found near Alice Springs.
The detective tipped his trilby and stepped into the rain.
Grandfather kept an old trilby on the hook by the door.
The lecture was given by Professor Helen Bixby of Yale.
Mr. Bixby owned the hardware store on Main Street.
The goal was scored by young Thomas Bibby in the last minute.
Uncle Digby arrived late with a suitcase full of books.
quiet: The greater bandicoot digs long burrows in the desert sand.
A colony of the rare wallaby was found near Alice Springs.
The detective tipped his fedora and stepped into the rain.
Grandfather kept an old derby on the hook by the door.
The lecture was given by Professor Helen Crosby of Yale.
Mr. Hornby owned the hardware store on Main Street.
The goal was scored by young Thomas Selby in the last minute.
Uncle Kirby arrived late with a suitcase full of books.

notes: Probes: bilby 0.88, Bixby 0.74, trilby 0.72, Bibby 0.62, Digby 0.41; Rigby 0.17; Libby, Selby, Hornby, Kirby, Crosby, wallaby and the preposition ' by' all near 0. The - pole is the stem ' bil' itself (bilinear, bilayer), so the + pole reads like 'by' completing a bil-/-i- stem. Some near-miss names may be single tokens, which is part of the point: the unit needs the split piece.
